title: Connection hold deadlock unwind and hosted API bridging
creator: Ava Patel
description: Customer escalation: multiple tenants reported sustained 500s and long tail timeouts during a traffic surge. Investigation traced pattern to connection pool starvation in the edge proxy combined with client-side aggressive retries and a KV cache eviction storm in the serving runtime. This ticket covers end-to-end RCA, immediate mitigations to stop customer-visible 5xx waves, and the staged production patch + follow-ups to prevent recurrence.
impact: High — several large customers experienced sustained request failures and elevated latency for 20–90 minutes during peak bursts. Practical impact included failed customer jobs, increased support escalations, and SLO breaches for hosted-api p95 latency and error-rate targets.
reproduction_steps: Simulate 3x baseline concurrent request load from a small set of tenant API keys (use loadgen script loadgen/tenant_burst.py)
Instrument client to retry on 5xx with exponential backoff disabled (to mimic aggressive SDK defaults) and high concurrency per connection
Observe edge-proxy connection pool exhaustion metrics (edge.conn_pool.active -> approaches limit) and rising queue depth on proxy request queues
Correlate with runtime logs showing KV cache compaction events and long GC-like pauses in the inference worker leading to increased per-request tail latency
Result: client retries amplify load -> proxy holds connections -> backend requests queue -> timeouts and 500s propagate
investigation: 12:10 — Pager triggered; assembled incident bridge (SRE, runtime, edge, SDK lead)
12:18 — Captured traces: long server-side spans in runtime.worker.process_request (500–2000ms extra on tail requests)
12:27 — Edge proxy metrics showed ephemeral surge of idle-but-held conns due to upstream slow responses; connection allocator hit soft limit and began queuing new requests
12:40 — Runtime logs revealed repeated KV cache compaction after short-lived memory pressure spikes caused by parallel batch allocations under burst workload
13:05 — Discovered correlation between retries without jitter and repeated identical prefixes causing KV cache churn and eviction storms in nodes pinned to small GPUs
13:20 — Identified two key contributors: (A) proxy admission + connection holding semantics; (B) SDK default retry/backoff semantics encouraging synchronous retry storms
mitigation: Deploy hotpatch to edge proxy (edge/patches/edge_0.9.7_hotfix): add short-circuit early-fail when connection pool below 10% capacity for non-idempotent endpoints
Enable per-tenant request shaping at proxy layer to cap burst concurrency to safe thresholds (config change, rolled to 3 regions)
Roll temporary runtime knob to increase KV cache eviction thresholds (reduce compaction aggressiveness) for 60 minutes while load subsided
Customer comms: PS team sent targeted status notes and advised customers to increase client-side jitter; SDK team published interim guidance to reduce concurrency and enable exponential jitter
Monitor: increased tracing sampling for affected tenants to 100% and added dashboard alert for pool saturation -> auto-runbook trigger
resolution: Hotpatch rolled at 13:48; error rates dropped within 7 minutes and p95 latency trended back to baseline by 14:10
Full patch (edge v0.9.8) merged: implements adaptive admission control with priority fastpath for high-SLA tenant keys and unified connection backoff across pooled clients (PR #1248)
Runtime change (runtime-1.24): improved KV cache prefetch heuristics and reduced compaction frequency for bursty prefix patterns (PR #1302)
SDK update published: default retry/backoff changed to randomized exponential backoff with min jitter and reduced default concurrency in node/python SDKs (SDK PRs #56, #59)
Post-mortem shared with customers and internal teams; incident closed after 72-hour monitoring window with no recurrence
follow_up_actions: ENG: implement automated tenant burst detection that triggers preemptive admission control (EPIC: tenant-burst-detection)
RUNTIME: add guardrail to throttle KV compaction when upstream queueing detected
EDGE: add metrics for per-connection hold time and expose in console (console-2025.03 roadmap)
SDK: include safety-mode option that opts into conservative retry semantics for production tenants
DOCS: create runbook excerpt for customer-facing support with reproducible steps and recommended SDK configurations
comments: Marcus Chen (2025-02-18): Deployed hotpatch to edge in us-east-1/us-west-2; watching error-rate and connection pool metrics. Edge CPU unchanged but queue depth down 60%.

Jules Nguyen (2025-02-18): Confirmed KV compaction spikes line up with per-node memory foot-print increases during parallel batch allocations; working on a conservative memory cap as intermediate fix.
Ava Patel (2025-02-19): SDK team will ship default backoff change and publish migration guidance; recommend customers upgrade within 2 weeks.
SRE Lead (2025-02-20): Added automated alert for edge.conn_pool.saturation -> runbook step added to temporarily divert tenant traffic to dedicated fallback pool.
Product (2025-02-22): Prioritizing long-term admission control epic in next planning cycle; mapping to dedicated capacity feature asks from 2 affected customers.
